messages:
ashwin: Heads-up — seeing a gradual +10-12% RSS growth over ~2 hours on Dedicated GPU pools when users run long-chat histories (~20k-30k tokens). Hosted traces look stable, Private looks intermittent. Dashboard: https://console.redwood/internal/kvcache/mem?run=171900

maria: ugh. is it steady linear growth or step-y jumps?

ashwin: fairly step-ish — correlates with page-in spikes in perf samples. Snapshot: `perf report` shows lots of time in `page_fault_handler` and `do_mmap`. Also see many anon_mmap regions for kv slabs.

jen: can you paste the allocation map? maybe jemalloc profiles?

ashwin: pasted below — small snippet from /proc/<pid>/maps and jemalloc stats (sanitized):
```
7f8a100000-7f8a200000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [anon]
7f8b300000-7f8b480000 rw-p 00000000 00:00 0                          [anon]
---
active: 4.6G allocated
mapped: 6.2G
metadata: 128M
```
perf sample line: `kernel:page_fault` flame indicates 45% of samples falling in kernel page fault path during hot batching.

sam: Dedicated nodes are on-prem colo with older NICs + VPC overlay vs Hosted (cloud native). Could VPC MTU or overlay be magnifying page fault handling due to networked IO for swap? We don't swap but our mmap-backed eviction touches hugepages/transparent huge page behavior.

maria: interesting. Private also on local NVMe in some customers — they don't show steady growth unless sequence lengths >40k. Maybe interaction between batching heuristics (longer prefixes) and KV slot reuse leading to fragmentation and more mmap churn.

ashwin: hypothesis: our KV cache eviction policy leaves many small free slots scattered -> future allocations cause new mmaps instead of reusing freed pages because of alignment/hugepage constraints on Dedicated kernels. Kernel config differs: Dedicated has THP=always and host uses 2MB hugepages set, Hosted is configured with THP=never and uses smaller mappings.

jen: can you repro with `MALLOC_CONF=lg_chunk:0,oversize_threshold:0` and `MADV_NOHUGEPAGE` toggles? Also capture `pagemap` churn: `watch -n1 cat /proc/<pid>/smaps | grep -E "AnonHugePages|Anon"`

ashwin: will run. quick test ran with MADV_NOHUGEPAGE on one dedicated node — immediate reduction in page_fault samples, RSS stabilized after ~20m.

perf-bot: perf regression check: compare commit range 8af1..b3d2, job 2026-03-10 showed small bump in mmap calls (x1.3) in kvcache allocator.

sam: that PR was kernel-affecting? I thought it touched allocator coalescing. If kvcache started aligning to 2MB boundaries for GPU DMA reasons, that could cause more internal fragmentation on kernels that don't back hugepages transparently.

maria: right — Dedicated images had a GPU alignment patch to map frames on 2MB boundaries to speed up memcpy to GPU. Works great on cloud hosts with THP=always but on our colocated Dedicated images it forces many extra anonymous mmaps and prevents jemalloc from reusing freed subregions. Hence growth.

jen: mitigation options: revert alignment change, enable MADV_HUGEPAGE proactively, or tweak eviction to eagerly coalesce free slots and return to kernel (munmap) instead of keeping as dirty arenas. Which is least risky?

ashwin: quick deploy plan: 1) roll MADV_NOHUGEPAGE -> we've already tested `MADV_NOHUGEPAGE` reduced pagefaults but that prevents hugepage use (bad perf for some models). 2) short-term: change allocator to prefer coalescing + munmap when free slab > X (config drift: hosted had X=256MB, Dedicated had X=1GB). 3) long-term: add kernel-detection path to pick hugepage strategy per node at startup.

sam: also check NIC/overlay MTU — we saw earlier on Dedicated that page fault latency was magnified by occasional network stalls during checkpointing to remote blobstore (async writeback hit). If eviction policy writes back metadata over the network, that could amplify.

ashwin: good catch. I saw `writeback` spikes aligned with some of the RSS jumps. I'll correlate IO stats and TSO/MTU logs.

maria: can you add a short repro script so infra can run on a couple Dedicated boxes? Keep it light: spawn long-chat load, force reuse pattern, toggles for `MADV_*` and allocation alignment env var.

ashwin: will open a small runbook + repro gist. For now, immediate experiment: lower `kv_coalesce_threshold` from 1G->128M on Dedicated pools and watch for RSS slope. If good, roll to all Dedicated as a mitigation while we implement kernel-aware strategy.

jen: sounds reasonable. please tag me on the runbook PR and add metrics to the kvcache dashboard for `AnonHugePages`, `mmap_calls`, and `page_fault_samples` so we can alert if slope > 5%/hr.

sam: also add a note for sales/solutions — Dedicated customers with older on-prem GPUs might see higher memory churn for long-context workloads until we ship fix.

ashwin: will do. quick TODOs: repro script + runbook (ashwin), infra experiment lowering coalesce (sam), dashboard metrics (jen), kernel detection shim prototype (maria). I'll post results in this thread. :thumbsup:
